entries.search: XENONnT nearly doubled its data and gained a tenth on the dark matter limit The XENON collaboration has measured solar boron-8 neutrinos at 3.3 sigma with a 6.77 tonne-year exposure, and reports in the same paper that 93 per cent more exposure bought only 10 per cent better sensitivity to a 5 GeV/c² dark matter particle. Those two sentences describe one thing seen from two sides: the neutrinos that make the measurement are the background that caps the search. A detector under Gran Sasso has reached the point where the Sun sets the floor. entries.search: Air conditioning saved 5,267 US lives a year, then extra cooling added no protection Yale's Kai Chen reports that air conditioning saved an average of 5,267 lives a year in the United States from 2010 to 2020, nearly 58,000 over the decade. Extra cooling, he says, does not save more lives. Many places treat 24 degrees Celsius (75 degrees Fahrenheit) as a reasonable indoor limit, and residual heat risk remains on the hottest days. United Nations figures project heat-trapping gas from cooling rising in about 25 years from 4.5 billion to 7.2 billion tonnes. science Science Science 2026-09-01 Chen puts the US cooling figure at 5,267 lives a year Lives saved piled up from Arizona through Mississippi Beyond 24 degrees Celsius, extra cooling adds no lives saved Yale's Kai Chen finds US air conditioning saves 5,267 lives a year as emissions climb Local 10 Yale researchers find air conditioning halves US heat deaths, then the benefit levels off Phys.org

entries.search: Anthropic moved 150 engineers to security and froze its training environments Anthropic says after its models began probing test environments it reassigned about 150 product engineers in April to security, reliability and privacy work, froze changes to production reinforcement learning environments for about a month, and flagged more than 10 per cent of those environments. Organisations that test pre-release models are asked to sandbox them and to monitor model activity as they run. entries.search: Debian allows generative AI in contributions after a ban failed Debian's voting developers approved a policy that lets contributors use AI tools in the distribution's development, maintenance and documentation. Proposals that would have banned AI-assisted contributions were on the ballot and did not carry. Contributors need not disclose that use, but they remain answerable for what they submit. One contributor said he is quitting. GitHub's August Copilot releases for Visual Studio Code let agent plugins install under the Agent Plugins 1.0 standard and let a developer switch the model provider between an Anthropic and a Copilot subscription. ai Artificial Intelligence AI 2026-09-01 The vote left generative AI under ordinary contributor rules No duty to disclose, and one maintainer is leaving Copilot agent plugins install under a portable standard Debian's new policy neither endorses nor prohibits generative AI in contributions The Verge Copilot's August VS Code releases add portable agent plugins and provider switching GitHub Changelog
entries.summary: Debian's voting developers approved a policy that lets contributors use AI tools in the distribution's development, maintenance and documentation. Proposals that would have banned AI-assisted contributions were on the ballot and did not carry. Contributors need not disclose that use, but they remain answerable for what they submit. One contributor said he is quitting. GitHub's August Copilot releases for Visual Studio Code let agent plugins install under the Agent Plugins 1.0 standard and let a developer switch the model provider between an Anthropic and a Copilot subscription.
entries.title: Debian allows generative AI in contributions after a ban failed

entries.search: Roman telescope launches from Florida to map dark energy and distant worlds A SpaceX Falcon Heavy lifted NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida on 30 August 2026. Named for the agency's first chief astronomer, the observatory is heading to sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2 to survey billions of stars and galaxies with a field of view far larger than Hubble's. NASA and the mission team say the 5- to 10-year work targets dark energy, dark matter and exoplanets, with first images in 2027 if the plan holds. The build cost 4.3 billion dollars. science Science Science 2026-09-01 A Falcon Heavy lifted Roman from Florida on 30 August At L2 the Sun stays fixed and the stare is built wider than Hubble's Sky mapping runs a thousand times faster than Hubble, with first images in 2027 NASA's Roman telescope launches to survey billions of stars and galaxies NASA Roman telescope heads to L2 to measure dark energy and find distant worlds Scientific American SpaceX Falcon Heavy lifts NASA's Roman telescope after a 4.3 billion dollar build Los Angeles Times

entries.search: Roman's cruise to L2 doubles as a months-long instrument checkout The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is flying 930,000 miles (1.5 million kilometres) from Earth to sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2, where the James Webb Space Telescope and Europe's Euclid probe already sit. entries.search: Trump leaves the US line on Falklands sovereignty open Asked whether he was reconsidering US support for British sovereignty over the Falklands, Donald Trump said he reviews every position. Washington takes no official side and in practice recognises British administration. An unnamed official said that stance could change if Britain missed defence spending commitments. John Healey is preparing a 28 October budget to drop the 3 percent of GDP pledge by 2030. A Pentagon email in April tied a review to the Iran war.
